title: Retail Installment Contracts and Collateral Protection Insurance: Insurance Allowance for Deferred Installments
content:
The insurance allowance for a hardship extension agreement on a contract under Retail Installment Contracts reads the vehicle's insurance tracking record kept under Collateral Protection Insurance: the record's current status, and the lapse notices mailed on it.

**Rule.**

- When the contract's insurance tracking record is **compliant** and no first or second lapse notice was mailed on it in the rolling 12 months ending on the signing date, the allowance is the tier's maximum installments deferred by one extension.
- When the contract's tracking record is **force-placed** or in **lapse-notice** status, the allowance is zero.
- In every other case it is **one** installment.

| Tracking record status | First or second lapse notice mailed in the rolling 12 months | Insurance allowance |
|---|---|---|
| compliant | none | the tier's per-request maximum |
| compliant | one or more | one installment |
| force-placed | any | zero |
| lapse notice | any | zero |
| any other status | any | one installment |

The rolling 12 months run from records dated later than the same calendar day 12 months before the signing date (the last day of that month when that day does not exist) through the signing date. Only notices of the first-lapse and second-lapse kinds are counted.

**Hypothetical case.** A tracking record now compliant again after the borrower sent proof of insurance, with a first lapse notice mailed four months before the signing date, gives an allowance of one installment; had that notice been mailed fourteen months before, the allowance would be the tier's per-request maximum.
